source_title: Temporary public policy to facilitate renewals of open work permits for foreign nationals in Canada who were facilitated under previous public policies for Haiti – Expires December 2027 - Canada.ca
source_excerpt:
Haiti continues to experience a severe humanitarian and security crisis, with widespread gang violence, displacement, and food insecurity affecting millions, including over 1.5 million internally displaced people and 5.8 million facing acute food shortages.
Many Haitians have chosen to come to Canada to visit or spend time with family, study, or work temporarily. Many foreign national family members of Canadian citizens or permanent residents who fled Haiti as a result of the crisis are in Canada on temporary status. Some of these temporary residents may be unable to return home due to the ongoing situation.
This temporary public policy continues facilitation for eligible foreign nationals from Haiti who are in Canada with temporary resident status. The measures outlined in this public policy will facilitate continued access to an open work permit renewals from within Canada, with standard fees, for foreign nationals from Haiti and foreign national family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents, who currently hold a work permit issued on the basis of exemptions under one of the previous public policies to support foreign nationals who left Haiti and who are in Canada as temporary residents.
Therefore, I hereby establish, pursuant to my authority under section 25.2 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the Act), that there are sufficient public policy considerations that justify the granting of an exemption from the provisions of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (the Regulations) to foreign nationals who meet the conditions (eligibility requirements) set out below.
Based on public policy considerations, delegated officers may grant an exemption from the requirements of the Regulations identified when a foreign national meets the following conditions:
The foreign national Has valid temporary resident status at the time the application is submitted and at the time a final decision is made; holds a valid work permit, at the time of application under c., issued on the basis of exemptions under one of the following public policies: Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents, signed on May 23, 2024 Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents – Extension, signed on November 19, 2024 Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents – Further extension, signed on November 19, 2025 Temporary Public Policy For Foreign Nationals Who Are Family Members Of Canadian Citizens And Permanent Residents Who Fled Violence In Haiti, signed on May 23, 2024 Temporary Public Policy for foreign nationals who are family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who fled violence in Haiti – Extension, signed on November 19, 2024 Updated temporary public policy for family members who fled violence in Haiti, signed on November 19, 2025 has applied from within Canada for a work permit renewal under subsection 201(1); and has not already been granted an exemption under the current public policy.
Has valid temporary resident status at the time the application is submitted and at the time a final decision is made;
holds a valid work permit, at the time of application under c., issued on the basis of exemptions under one of the following public policies: Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents, signed on May 23, 2024 Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents – Extension, signed on November 19, 2024 Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents – Further extension, signed on November 19, 2025 Temporary Public Policy For Foreign Nationals Who Are Family Members Of Canadian Citizens And Permanent Residents Who Fled Violence In Haiti, signed on May 23, 2024 Temporary Public Policy for foreign nationals who are family members of Canadian citizens and permanent residents who fled violence in Haiti – Extension, signed on November 19, 2024 Updated temporary public policy for family members who fled violence in Haiti, signed on November 19, 2025
Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents, signed on May 23, 2024
Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents – Extension, signed on November 19, 2024
Temporary public policy for Haitian nationals in Canada as temporary residents – Further extension, signed on November 19, 2025
Temporary Public Policy For Foreign Nationals Who Are Family Members Of Canadian Citizens And Permanent Residents Who Fled Violence In Haiti, signed on May 23, 2024

has applied from within Canada for a work permit renewal under subsection 201(1); and

Provisions of the Regulations for which an exemption may be granted:
For foreign nationals who meet the conditions listed above
Paragraph 200(1)(c) – the requirement to be described under this paragraph of the Regulations
Other Admissibility and Selection Criteria
Foreign nationals eligible under this public policy are subject to all other applicable eligibility and admissibility requirements not otherwise exempted.
This public policy comes into effect on October 28, 2026 and will expire on December 30, 2027. This public policy may be revoked at any time without prior notice.
Applications received pursuant to this public policy on or after the coming into effect date and before the expiry date, or the revocation of the public policy, will be processed under this public policy.
The Hon. Lena Metlege Diab, ECNS, KC, P.C., M.P. Minister of Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Dated at Ottawa, this 26th day of October 2026
